title: Illiquid Assets

maps.tested: Rated Very Important; reported once as a named question.
maps.specifics: Reported: 'illiquid asset question.' Examinable: the biases in reported illiquid-asset returns (survivorship, sample selection, infrequent trading and the resulting understated volatility and correlation), illiquidity risk premiums, and portfolio allocation with illiquid assets.

vardeezReading: IM-17: Very Important; LO 99.e and LO 99.f are Important.

selectors.name: Biases in reported illiquid returns, unsmoothing
selectors.what: The three biases in reported illiquid-asset returns (survivorship, selection, infrequent trading), their direction, the matching correction (unsmoothing for infrequent trading, Heckman for selection, the full population for survivorship), and the unsmoothing filter and what it changes: r_t = (r*_t - phi x r*_(t-1)) / (1 - phi), where reported returns follow r*_t = c + phi x r*_(t-1) + e_t.
selectors.theory: All three biases overstate expected returns and understate risk. Reported returns are a weighted average of the true return and the lagged reported return, r*_t = (1 - phi) r_t + phi r*_(t-1), so unsmoothing inverts this: it raises volatility, correlation and beta (true variance exceeds reported variance when |phi| < 1), leaves the mean unchanged, and has no effect when phi = 0.

selectors.name: Illiquidity premiums: across versus within classes
selectors.what: Whether illiquidity risk premiums are found across asset classes (conventional view, flawed: biases, other risks, no investable index, skill versus factor risk) or within asset classes (on-the-run versus off-the-run, bond yields, equities, private equity secondaries), and the four ways to harvest them: passive allocation, liquidity security selection, market making, dynamic rebalancing (simplest, greatest impact).

selectors.name: Portfolio allocation with illiquid assets
selectors.what: Optimal holdings of illiquid assets and the premiums required: the no-trade band under transaction costs (Constantinides), the optimal holding falling and the required premium rising as the average interval between liquidity events (1/lambda) lengthens, and the rebalancing point, which is below the long-run average holding.

notSelected: IM-17 a (characteristics of illiquid markets) and IM-17 b (market imperfections and the sources of illiquidity) carry no shape, no Map point and no Vardeez pointer; the Harvard endowment case is background only.
